final_response:
I read this as a read-only root-cause report for the three Ferryx drag/drop symptoms - I traced geometry, native-webview behavior, callback wiring, reducers, and the QA path that falsely passed.

## Verdict

There are **three independent root causes**, plus one rejected hypothesis:

1. **Small-strip feedback is explicitly implemented as 20% edge geometry, not half-pane feedback.**
2. **The native browser child webview remains visible during DnD and sits outside the React document/layer, so browser-content drag tracking and overlays stop at the React address-bar region.**
3. **Dragging the active terminal tab onto its own visible pane resolves as a tab move, but the store intentionally rejects source-tab === target-tab, making the drop a silent no-op.**
4. **Missing App/store prop wiring is not the cause**; the necessary callbacks are wired.

These collectively explain all reported symptoms.

---

## 1. Confirmed: pane feedback is designed as a 20% strip

`SplitEdgeDropZone` uses the same element for both collision detection and visible feedback:

- `ui/src/components/tab-dnd/SplitEdgeDropZone.tsx:45-48`
- `ui/src/components/tab-dnd/SplitEdgeDropZone.tsx:63-72`

Exact geometry:

```tsx
left/right: w-[20%]
top/bottom: h-[20%]
```

The active highlight is applied directly to that 20%-sized element:

```tsx
isOver && "border-2 border-primary bg-primary/20 ..."
```

The production group-edge surface independently repeats the same geometry:

- `ui/src/components/tab-dnd/TabGroupDropSurface.tsx:48-54`

Therefore the reported “small strips instead of half-pane” is not a collision bug. It is the literal rendered CSS.

### Unfaithful QA

`ui/src/components/tab-dnd/SplitEdgeDropZone.test.tsx:47-51` explicitly blesses the wrong behavior:

```tsx
expect(groupEdge.className).toBe(paneEdge.className);
expect(groupEdge).toHaveClass("inset-y-0", "left-0", "w-[20%]");
expect(paneEdge).toHaveClass("inset-y-0", "left-0", "w-[20%]");
```

The test proves that group and pane feedback are equally narrow; it never proves half-pane coverage. The retained screenshots also visibly show narrow strips, despite `ORCA_TAB_SPLIT_TERMINAL_RUNTIME_FIX_REPORT.md` claiming the overlay “covers the corresponding half.”

### Smallest correct fix seam

Keep the 20% collision target if desired, but separate it from the visual preview:

- Invisible/ref-bearing hit region: 20%.
- Conditional sibling preview: 50% of the target pane.
  - left/right: full height, half width.
  - top/bottom: full width, half height.

Do not simply enlarge the droppable unless changing edge activation sensitivity is intended.

Test seam:

```text
SplitEdgeDropZone renders a 20% hit target and a distinct 50% pane preview
```

Assert separate DOM nodes/classes rather than identical classes. A browser-layout test should additionally compare preview and pane bounding rectangles at `0.5` width/height.

---

## 2. High-confidence native root cause: browser child webview blocks React DnD

The browser has two different rendering surfaces:

- React toolbar/address bar in the main Ferryx webview:
  - `ui/src/components/BrowserPane.tsx:57-64`
  - `ui/src/components/BrowserToolbar.tsx:87-127`
- Native Tauri child webview occupying only `browser-viewport`:
  - bounds measured at `ui/src/components/BrowserPane.tsx:30-37`
  - child created at `src-tauri/src/ipc/browser.rs:50-57`
  - native bounds applied at `src-tauri/src/ipc/browser.rs:100-119`

`TerminalSplitView` always renders the active browser as visible:

- `ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:656-663`

There is no drag-state prop that hides the native child.

This matters because dnd-kit’s pointer sensor listens on the owner document of the React drag source:

- `ui/node_modules/@dnd-kit/core/dist/core.esm.js:1411-1438`

The Tauri child webview is not a DOM descendant of that document; it is a separate native webview. Once the pointer crosses from the React toolbar into the native browser viewport:

- React no longer receives normal pointer movement/up events from that child surface.
- React `z-40` feedback cannot reliably composite above the native child.
- The last visible/trackable region is the React browser toolbar/address-bar area.
- The final `over` can remain stale, become null, or the parent document may not receive pointer-up at all.

That causally matches both:

- “browser feedback appears in address-bar area”
- browser-surface drops doing nothing

### Why the existing QA was unfaithful

The report says Chromium QA exercised the “shipped” surface, but the screenshots contain:

> Launch through Tauri to attach the PTY session.

That text is emitted only outside Tauri:

- `ui/src/lib/terminalInstanceFactory.ts:179-182`

The report also records a temporary Vite QA page and Playwright Chromium, not a native Ferryx run. Consequently, that QA had:

- no Tauri `add_child` webview;
- no native compositing layer;
- no native input boundary;
- only a DOM browser placeholder.

The automated browser tests are equally unable to catch this:

- `ui/src/components/BrowserPane.test.tsx:32-51` mocks `setBrowserBounds` and `setBrowserVisible`.
- It even accepts a zero-sized jsdom rectangle.
- `ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.browserPaneDrop.runtime.test.tsx:14-45` mocks all of dnd-kit.
- That test manually calls `onDragStart` and `onDragEnd` at lines 129-154, bypassing pointer movement and the native-webview boundary entirely.

### Smallest correct fix seam

Hide active native browser child webviews for the duration of any workspace drag:

1. On DnD start, render every mounted `BrowserPane` with `visible={false}`.
2. On drag end/cancel, restore visibility for active browser panes.
3. Keep the React browser placeholder mounted so it becomes the pointer/collision surface.
4. Continue using the existing per-browser visibility queue in:
   - `ui/src/lib/browserTauri.ts:9-24`
   - `ui/src/lib/browserTauri.ts:42-43`

The smallest component-level approach is to pass an `isWorkspaceDragging` value through `TabGroupView` and use:

```tsx
<BrowserPane visible={!isWorkspaceDragging} ... />
```

Test seam:

```text
TerminalSplitView hides native browser webviews on drag start and restores them on drag cancel/end
```

Mock `setBrowserVisible` and assert `true -> false -> true`. That proves lifecycle coordination, but one real Tauri desktop test remains necessary to prove native z-order and pointer continuity.

---

## 3. Confirmed: active-tab self-drop is routed into a reducer no-op

For an active terminal tab, its own pane is the pane currently rendered. Dropping that tab on its pane edge resolves to:

```tsx
move-tab-to-pane-split
```

Evidence:

- `ui/src/components/tab-dnd/tabDragTypes.ts:157-168`

`TerminalSplitView` then always forwards terminal sources to `onMoveTabToSplit` with a target pane:

- `ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx:268-290`

The store dispatches `MOVE_TAB_TO_PANE_SPLIT`:

- `ui/src/state/workspaceStore.ts:349-369`
- `ui/src/state/workspaceStore.ts:990-1002`

But the underlying transition immediately rejects a self-target:

- `ui/src/state/tabPaneDrop.ts:30-31`

```tsx
if (sourceTabId === targetTabId) return state;
```

So the causal path is:

1. Drag active tab.
2. Hover its visible pane edge.
3. Resolver creates a valid-looking command.
4. `executeDrop` returns `true` merely because the callback exists.
5. Store receives source tab and target tab with the same ID.
6. `moveTabIntoPaneSplit` returns unchanged state.
7. User sees no layout change and no error.

The implementation report itself states the intended behavior was different: a self-pane drop should call `onSplitPane` and create a new PTY in that exact leaf. The current source does not implement that branch.

### Why QA missed it

The pane-target resolver test only proves command construction:

- `ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx:105-122`

It explicitly constructs a same-tab command but never executes it against the store.

The store pane-drop test only covers different tabs:

- `ui/src/state/workspaceStore.paneDrop.runtime.test.tsx:107-122`
- source is `tab-source`;
- target is `tab-target`.

The visual Chromium screenshot dragged `main (2)` onto the visible `main` pane. That is a cross-tab move, not the ordinary active-tab self-drop.

### Smallest correct fix seam

In `TerminalSplitView.executeDrop`, before forwarding a terminal `move-tab-to-pane-split`:

```tsx
if (command.sourceTabId === command.targetTabId) {
  onSplitPane(
    command.targetTabId,
    command.targetLeafId,
    command.direction,
    { position: command.position },
  );
  return true;
}
```

Only different terminal tabs should use `onMoveTabToSplit(..., targetPane)`.

Failing-first test:

```text
TerminalSplitView splits the exact hovered leaf when the active tab is dropped on its own pane edge
```

Assertions:

- `onSplitPane(tabId, leafId, direction, { position })` called once.
- `onMoveTabToSplit` not called.
- Store-level follow-up asserts one backend terminal is spawned and the selected leaf becomes a 0.5 split.

---

## 4. Rejected hypothesis: App callback wiring is missing

The real App supplies all relevant callbacks:

- `onMoveTabToGroup={moveTabToGroup}` — `ui/src/App.tsx:807`
- `onMoveTabToSplit={moveTabToSplit}` — `ui/src/App.tsx:808`
- `onDetachPaneToTab={detachPaneToTab}` — `ui/src/App.tsx:809`
- `onSplitPane={handleSplitPane}` — `ui/src/App.tsx:820`

Cross-tab store transitions are also implemented and covered:

- pane-tree move: `ui/src/state/tabPaneDrop.ts:21-100`
- browser group split: `ui/src/state/layout.ts:315-363`

So the general failure is not caused by absent production props.

However, `App.test.tsx` mocks `TerminalSplitView` at `ui/src/App.test.tsx:222-265` and does not capture or exercise these DnD props. That App-level test would not detect future wiring regressions.

---

## Symptom-to-cause mapping

| Reported symptom | Causal root |
|---|---|
| Pane-edge feedback is only a small strip | The highlighted droppable itself is hard-coded to 20%, not 50%. |
| Browser feedback appears around the address bar | The address bar is React, while the viewport is a native child webview that remains above/outside the React DnD surface. |
| Browser-content drop does nothing | Parent dnd-kit pointer tracking/pointer-up cannot reliably continue through the native child webview. |
| Active terminal tab drop does nothing | Self-pane command is forwarded to `moveTabIntoPaneSplit`, which rejects identical source/target tab IDs. |
| Cross-tab store tests pass | They bypass native input and use different source/target IDs, so neither real-app failure is exercised. |

## Verification performed

Read-only focused verification passed:

```text
6 test files passed
9 tests passed
```

Those passing tests reinforce the QA gap: they pass while explicitly pinning 20% feedback, mocking dnd-kit, mocking native browser IPC, and avoiding same-tab execution. No files were edited.
